name: Hydroa Vacciniforme-Like Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, histopathological, and virological findings

criteria.description: Recurrent vesiculopapular eruptions on sun-exposed skin with subsequent vacciniform scarring
Skin biopsy showing atypical cytotoxic T-cell infiltrate with angiocentric and angiodestructive features
Detection of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in lesional skin by in situ hybridization or PCR
Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement and cytotoxic T-cell immunophenotype (CD8+, CD56 variable)
Presence of systemic symptoms or organ involvement supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions with histopathological confirmation and EBV positivity in skin lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, and virological data; differentiation from other EBV-associated lymphoproliferative disorders is essential

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent vesiculopapular eruptions on sun-exposed skin
pathognomonic.notes: Lesions typically progress to necrosis and vacciniform scarring
searchTerms: repeated blistering rashes on sun-exposed skin
vesicle and papule outbreaks after sun exposure

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic pock-like scars on exposed areas
searchTerms: scars resembling vaccine marks after lesions heal

common.symptomName: Facial edema associated with skin lesions
searchTerms: swelling of face with skin lesions
facial puffiness linked to skin problems
edematous face associated with skin eruptions

common.notes: Regional or generalized lymph node enlargement

searchTerms: skin lesions worsen with sun exposure

occasional.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen in some cases
Painful ulcers may occur in the oral cavity

rare.notes: Rare cases with CNS infiltration causing neurological deficits
Severe immune activation syndrome in advanced disease
Rare lung infiltration by lymphoma cells

laboratory: Elevated EBV viral load in peripheral blood
imaging: CT or MRI showing lymphadenopathy and organomegaly
Skin lesion imaging rarely used but may show subcutaneous involvement
genetic: Clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement detected by PCR
other: Positive EBV-encoded RNA (EBER) in situ hybridization in skin biopsy
Immunophenotyping showing cytotoxic T-cell markers (CD8+, TIA-1+, granzyme B+)

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of EBV positivity in lesions
No atypical lymphoid infiltrate on biopsy
Predominantly nasal and midline facial involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with ulceration
Development of systemic symptoms such as persistent high fever and weight loss
references: Kimura H, et al. Hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoma: a distinct EBV-associated lymphoproliferative disorder of childhood. Blood. 2008.
Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Orphanet: Hydroa vacciniforme-like lymphoma. Orphanet Report Series; 2023.
